pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage has stepped up and has not stabilised. Net debt to LTM EBITDA was 1.39x at year-end 2025, 2.00x at September 30, 2026 and is 2.48x pro forma for the Paloma closing on October 1, 2026, because the federal lease, Cardinal and Paloma purchases were funded with cash and borrowings while LTM EBITDA rose only 1.51%; management intends to repay between $350 million and $400 million by year-end, of which $150 million was repaid by November 3, 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_a20260930mtdr8ker-ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C14

- Cash generation covers interest but not the acquisition programme. Free cash flow after organic capital spending was USD 688,366 thousand over the last twelve months, equal to 0.28x of EBITDA, against nine-month 2026 acquisition spending of USD 2,102,218 thousand and organic free cash flow of USD 724,669 thousand, so the difference was debt-funded and interest cover has fallen from 15.03x in FY2024 to 11.29x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1

- Liquidity is adequate today but thin after Paloma. Reported liquidity of USD 1,832,829 thousand at September 30, 2026 included USD 1,745,941 thousand undrawn on the Credit Agreement, which falls to about $446.9 million on borrowings of $2.25 billion, and the borrowing base of $3.25 billion leaves a cushion of $946.9 million before a deficiency; the result of the November 1, 2026 redetermination is not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C3; calculation C4

- The hedge book protects little of the downside and has already cost cash. Oil collars for the fourth quarter of 2026 have a ceiling of $66.36 per barrel against a third-quarter realized price of $87.25, realized derivative losses were USD 247,151 thousand in the nine months, the net derivative liability was USD 203,691 thousand, and floors cover 48.91% of expected fourth quarter oil but the 2027 collars cover only 7.75% of a year's oil at 2026 guidance volumes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_a20260930mtdr8ker-ex991.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C5; calculation C6

- Structure and maturities add a second pressure point. San Mateo carries USD 1,649,266 thousand of non-recourse debt, 33.20% of carrying-value debt, including a $650.0 million term loan due July 30, 2027 that is to be refinanced without assurance, while 49% of San Mateo's distributions leave the Matador group. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C11

- Business quality is the main support. Production grew 10% year on year in the third quarter, proved reserves give a reserve life of 8.8 years, and an integrated midstream system, a 2026 notes refinancing that moved the 2028 maturity to 2034 and a Fitch rating raised to BB give access to capital that a smaller single-basin producer would lack. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_mtdr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_mtdr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Financial policy is shareholder-friendly during a leverage build. The quarterly dividend was raised by 16.67% on October 21, 2026, which implies about $216.56 million a year, or 31.46% of last twelve months organic free cash flow, while seller relationships with EnCap-linked companies recur across the acquisitions and governance documents were not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C9

runs.text: Ranked strengths. First, scale and reserve life: production of 230,470 BOE per day and reserves of 667.0 million BOE give a reserve life of 8.8 years, which spreads fixed costs and supports lender confidence in the borrowing base. Second, cash generation: LTM EBITDA of USD 2,474,028 thousand covers cash interest 11.29x, so a revenue shock must be large before interest is at risk. Third, integrated midstream: 720 MMcf per day of processing at San Mateo plus Cardinal gives flow assurance and fee income. Fourth, market access: the 2028 notes were replaced with 2034 notes at a 6.0% coupon and the Credit Agreement commitment was raised to $2.75 billion, so refinancing in 2026 was achievable. Fifth, reporting quality: effective controls and quarterly reconciliations support monitoring. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_mtdr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_mtdr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

Ranked weaknesses. First, acquisition-driven leverage: pro forma net debt of USD 6,147.402 million is 2.48x LTM EBITDA, so earnings from the acquired assets must arrive to restore the year-end 2025 level of 1.39x. Second, revolver headroom: about $446.9 million undrawn after Paloma leaves little room for a further shock. Third, hedge structure: ceilings below the realized price turn higher prices into cash losses while floors protect only part of the volume. Fourth, structural leakage and maturity at San Mateo: 33.20% of debt is non-recourse, 49% of distributions go to the partner and $650.0 million falls due on July 30, 2027. Fifth, concentration in one basin, one commodity and three purchasers. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; calculation C3; calculation C5

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Matador completed or agreed four acquisitions in 2026 and financed them with a mix of cash, borrowings and new debt. In May 2026 it bought 5,154 net undeveloped acres in the Delaware Basin through the federal lease sale for about $1.16 billion; on July 31, 2026 San Mateo bought the operating subsidiaries of Cardinal Midstream Partners for $761.0 million in cash, funded by a new $650.0 million term loan due July 30, 2027, capital contributions of $51.0 million from Matador and $49.0 million from Five Point, and cash on hand; and on October 1, 2026 Matador closed the purchase of Paloma Permian for an as-adjusted price of about USD 1,255 million, against USD 1,275 million agreed on July 22, 2026, using cash and Credit Agreement borrowings. The Ridge Runner purchase of 13,600 net acres in the Woodford play was agreed on July 22, 2026 with subsidiaries of Ridge Runner Resources II, an EnCap portfolio company, expected to be funded by cash on hand and Credit Agreement borrowings, and is stated to have closed in October 2026, with no price disclosed. The price of Cardinal was stated as $752.0 million in the second quarter report and as $761.0 million in the third quarter report, both subject to post-closing adjustments. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mtdr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_a20260630mtdr8ker-ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_a20260930mtdr8ker-ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_a20260930mtdr8ker-ex991.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C10

The new debt issues in 2026 were a $750.0 million 6.0% senior unsecured note due April 15, 2034, sold on March 5, 2026 with net proceeds of $737.1 million, and the $650.0 million San Mateo term loan. The notes funded the tender offer for $419.8 million of the $500.0 million 2028 notes and the redemption of the remaining $80.2 million on April 15, 2026, at a cost of $15.6 million in lost premium and written-off issuance costs, and the Credit Agreement commitments were raised from $2.25 billion to $2.75 billion in June 2026 with the borrowing base reaffirmed at $3.25 billion. After the tender and redemption the refinancing added net new funding of about $227.4 million, and the maturity of that portion of the debt moved from 2028 to 2034. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C11

fields.value: Net debt to LTM EBITDA rose from 1.39x at year-end 2025 to 2.00x at September 30, 2026, and pro forma for the Paloma acquisition closed on October 1, 2026 it is 2.48x, so creditors now rely on acquired production arriving on plan.

Interest cover is still 11.29x, but Credit Agreement borrowings of $951.0 million at quarter end reached $2.25 billion by November 3, 2026, leaving about $446.9 million of undrawn capacity. The 2.48x pro forma figure divides by reported EBITDA that holds almost none of the acquired earnings.

The step-up is an acquisition effect, not an operating one, because reported EBITDA over the last twelve months rose from USD 2,437,322 thousand to USD 2,474,028 thousand while carrying-value debt rose from USD 3,402,102 thousand to USD 4,967,908 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three 2026 transactions explain the debt. The May 2026 federal lease purchase cost about $1.16 billion and was funded from cash and Credit Agreement borrowings, San Mateo bought Cardinal Midstream on July 31, 2026 for $761.0 million using a new $650.0 million term loan, and Matador replaced its $500.0 million 6.875% 2028 notes with $750.0 million of 6.0% 2034 notes in March 2026. Credit Agreement borrowings rose from USD 398,000 thousand to USD 951,000 thousand and the San Mateo revolver from USD 883,000 thousand to USD 1,002,000 thousand, so borrowing, not retained cash, funded most of the acquisition cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover on cash interest remains comfortable but is falling as debt is added: reported EBITDA to cash interest was 15.03x in FY2024, 12.41x in FY2025 and 11.29x over the last twelve months. Cash interest paid over that period was USD 219,121 thousand against USD 196,368 thousand in FY2025, and the run-rate is likely to rise further because the cost of the Cardinal term loan (an effective rate of 6.91%) and the post-quarter Credit Agreement borrowing are not yet in the history.

fields.value: Organic cash generation is modest relative to EBITDA because capital spending absorbs most of it, and it does not cover the acquisition programme. Net cash from operations was USD 2,476,555 thousand over the last twelve months and cash flow after drilling, midstream and other organic capital spending was USD 688,366 thousand, equal to 0.28x of reported EBITDA, while nine-month 2026 acquisition spending on properties, Cardinal and the Paloma deposit totalled USD 2,102,218 thousand against organic free cash flow of USD 724,669 thousand. The difference was debt-funded, which is why net debt rose faster than EBITDA.

fields.value: The hedge book is a cash cost at current prices and a growing liability. Realized derivative losses were USD 247,151 thousand in the nine months to September 30, 2026 against a gain of USD 13,607 thousand a year earlier, driven by a realized oil loss of USD 374,285 thousand partly offset by a natural gas gain of USD 127,134 thousand, and the net derivative liability on the balance sheet was USD 203,691 thousand against a net asset of USD 34,052 thousand at year-end 2025. Reported EBITDA deducts the unrealized loss of USD 237,744 thousand, while the issuer's adjusted figure adds it back but still bears the realized loss, so the two EBITDA definitions differ by USD 266,022 thousand for the last twelve months, of which USD 207,370 thousand is the unrealized derivative result.

fields.value: Royalties payable are a large non-debt funding float that the liquidity view should not treat as ordinary payables. They stood at USD 378,406 thousand at September 30, 2026, up from USD 351,062 thousand at year-end 2025 and USD 227,865 thousand at year-end 2024, and advances from joint interest owners add USD 79,564 thousand; both are interest-free obligations to owners that fund operations, so a slowdown in revenue or a settlement catch-up would draw on the revolver rather than on retained cash.

fields.value: Reported liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 1,832,829 thousand: cash of USD 11,756 thousand plus USD 1,745,941 thousand undrawn on the Credit Agreement and USD 75,132 thousand on the San Mateo revolver, which is available only inside San Mateo. After the Paloma purchase, the Credit Agreement stood at about $2.25 billion of borrowings against commitments of $2.75 billion and letters of credit of about $53.1 million at quarter end, which leaves roughly $446.9 million undrawn, so near-term flexibility depends on the stated plan to repay between $350 million and $400 million by year-end, of which $150 million was repaid by November 3, 2026.

fields.value: The next maturity is San Mateo's $650.0 million term loan due July 30, 2027, shown as a current liability of USD 647,266 thousand, and San Mateo says it expects to refinance it but gives no assurance. Without a refinancing, San Mateo would use cash, operating cash flow, the revolver (with USD 75,132 thousand undrawn) and member contributions, so a refinancing failure would fall partly on Matador as the owner of 51% of San Mateo. The remaining principal falls due in 2029 (USD 1,953,000 thousand across two revolvers) and in 2032, 2033 and 2034 (USD 2,400,000 thousand of senior unsecured notes).

fields.value: Business and governance review of Matador Resources Co (issuer mtdr-1520006), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance risk is medium: a founder-led single-basin producer is funding four 2026 acquisitions largely with borrowings while raising its dividend, so creditors rely on integration succeeding and on a stated debt repayment plan.

fields.value: The company was founded in 2003 and is led by one Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and 72% of 2025 oil, natural gas and NGL revenue came from three purchasers. San Mateo is 51% owned and consolidated but carries its own non-recourse debt, and about 49% of its distributions go to the partner, so cash leaves the group before it can service parent debt. Director independence, ownership and related-party details sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, which limits the governance view.

fields.value: - Governance information is thin where creditors need it, and continuity is mixed. Board composition, independence, ownership and related-party matters are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer roles are combined, the officer signing as Chief Financial Officer differed in each of the 2024 annual report, the 2025 annual report and the March 2026 quarterly report, and the Executive Vice President for Midstream resigned effective September 2, 2026. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure and controls are a strength for monitoring. The company files annual and quarterly reports with reconciliations of adjusted measures, its auditor has served since 2014 and attested internal control over financial reporting, and management reported effective disclosure controls at September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk view is the stated deleveraging intent and the operating record: management says it expects to repay between $350 million and $400 million of Credit Agreement borrowings by year-end, of which $150 million was repaid by November 3, 2026, third-quarter capital spending of $381 million was 10% below guidance, Fitch upgraded the company to BB in 2025, and the March 2026 notes refinancing retired the 2028 notes through a cash tender and redemption rather than an exchange. The supplied documents show no drop-down, priming transaction or exchange of notes, and the three supplemental indentures dated November 3, 2026 appear in the exhibit list for the notes after the Paloma closing, which is consistent with the acquired entities joining the notes' guarantee group, although their terms were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve to low if the repayment plan is met without a further debt-funded acquisition, the proxy statement shows a board with a majority of independent directors and no related-party leakage, and the San Mateo term loan due July 30, 2027 is refinanced on a long-term basis. It would worsen to high if shareholder payouts continue to rise while Credit Agreement borrowings stay near $2.25 billion, if the term loan cannot be refinanced and members must fund it, or if the governing documents show capacity for drop-downs or priming that the filings do not describe.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Matador completed or agreed four acquisitions in 2026 and financed them with a mix of cash, borrowings and new debt. In May 2026 it bought 5,154 net undeveloped acres in the Delaware Basin through the federal lease sale for about $1.16 billion; on July 31, 2026 San Mateo bought the operating subsidiaries of Cardinal Midstream Partners for $761.0 million in cash, funded by a new $650.0 million term loan due July 30, 2027, capital contributions of $51.0 million from Matador and $49.0 million from Five Point, and cash on hand; and on October 1, 2026 Matador closed the purchase of Paloma Permian for an as-adjusted price of about USD 1,255 million, against USD 1,275 million agreed on July 22, 2026, using cash and Credit Agreement borrowings. The Ridge Runner purchase of 13,600 net acres in the Woodford play was agreed on July 22, 2026 with subsidiaries of Ridge Runner Resources II, an EnCap portfolio company, expected to be funded by cash on hand and Credit Agreement borrowings, and is stated to have closed in October 2026, with no price disclosed. The price of Cardinal was stated as $752.0 million in the second quarter report and as $761.0 million in the third quarter report, both subject to post-closing adjustments.

fields.value: Fundamental credit review of Matador Resources Co (issuer mtdr-1520006), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the integrated credit view built on the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work, tested against the supplied annual reports, quarterly reports and earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit quality is adequate but weaker than at year-end 2025: pro forma net debt to LTM EBITDA is 2.48x after Paloma closed on October 1, 2026 and revolver headroom has narrowed, so creditors depend on oil prices and a repayment plan.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is large and cash generative, with LTM EBITDA covering cash interest 11.29x and a reserve life of 8.8 years, but the 2026 acquisitions were mostly borrowed: Credit Agreement borrowings rose from $951.0 million at quarter end to $2.25 billion by November 3, 2026, leaving about $446.9 million undrawn. Reverting to the 2025 average oil price would put pro forma net leverage between 3.01x and 3.40x before management actions.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mtdr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C2; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage has stepped up and has not stabilised. Net debt to LTM EBITDA was 1.39x at year-end 2025, 2.00x at September 30, 2026 and is 2.48x pro forma for the Paloma closing on October 1, 2026, because the federal lease, Cardinal and Paloma purchases were funded with cash and borrowings while LTM EBITDA rose only 1.51%; management intends to repay between $350 million and $400 million by year-end, of which $150 million was repaid by November 3, 2026.

fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate today but thin after Paloma. fields.value: - Business quality is the main support. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weakening view is management's own expectation that its leverage ratio will approach 1.5x by year-end 2026 and, as stated in August, reach about 1.0x by the end of 2027, funded mainly by free cash flow, with adjusted free cash flow of $287.6 million in the third quarter and Paloma and Ridge Runner adding production from the fourth quarter. Dividing pro forma net debt by annualised third-quarter consolidated adjusted EBITDA gives 1.96x, and the oil price realized in the third quarter of $87.25 per barrel is above the last twelve months average of $79.63. The definition behind management's ratio is not supplied and it is not reproduced here: reaching 1.5x on LTM reported EBITDA would need net debt $2,436.36 million lower than the pro forma figure, of which the stated repayment plan covers 16.42%.

fields.value: The view would improve if revolver repayments reach the stated range with no further debt-funded acquisition, if the November 1, 2026 redetermination leaves the borrowing base at or above $3.25 billion, and if the San Mateo term loan is refinanced long term before its 2027 maturity. It would worsen if realized oil prices fall toward the 2025 average of $64.99 per barrel while collar ceilings still absorb cash, if the borrowing base is cut below drawn amounts, or if dividends and acquisitions continue to rise while borrowings stay near $2.25 billion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Matador is a founder-led independent oil and natural gas producer that drills for oil in the Wolfcamp and Bone Spring formations of the Delaware Basin, supplemented by Haynesville and Cotton Valley gas, and owns 51% of the San Mateo midstream venture. The Delaware Basin supplied 100% of oil production and 97% of natural gas production in the third quarter of 2026, production was 230,470 BOE per day, and reserves were 667.0 million BOE at the end of 2025 with 61% proved developed. Because Matador sells at market prices, revenue is a function of price and volume: oil provided 76.84% of FY2025 revenue and third-party midstream fees only 4.46%, so cash-flow visibility depends on price and on the hedges that currently cap upside more than they protect downside. Debt service capacity is supported by LTM EBITDA of USD 2,474,028 thousand against cash interest of USD 219,121 thousand, and refinancing confidence by a 2026 market refinancing, but the 2026 acquisition programme has added debt faster than earnings.

fields.value: Matador is a public company with no controlling shareholder identified in the supplied documents; board, ownership and related-party details sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Debt sits in two separate silos: the Credit Agreement borrower, MRC Energy Company, is guaranteed by the parent and by subsidiaries, the senior notes are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, and San Mateo, owned 51% by Matador and 49% by Five Point, is neither a note guarantor nor a Credit Agreement guarantor and borrows on its own non-recourse facility. This means 33.20% of consolidated debt ranks against San Mateo's assets only, 49% of its distributions leave the group, and parent creditors rely on Matador's 51% share. Financial policy shows rising dividends, a repurchase authority of USD 320,195 thousand and acquisition-led growth, with controls effective and reporting timely, which makes the policy transparent but not conservative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is price-driven, cyclical and concentrated rather than contracted. Oil revenue rose 36% in the nine months to September 30, 2026 as the realized oil price reached $87.25 per barrel in the third quarter against $64.91 a year earlier, while natural gas revenue fell 56% because the second quarter realization was negative at USD 0.79 per Mcf before the Hugh Brinson pipeline began service on September 1, 2026. Three purchasers took 72% of 2025 oil, natural gas and NGL revenue, so a purchaser failure or a price shock reaches revenue directly, and the realized price after derivatives of $74.84 per barrel shows that collars with a ceiling of $66.36 transfer upside to counterparties. The implication is that revenue durability is average: volume growth of 10% and pipeline access support it, but price exposure and purchaser concentration limit visibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are partly variable and partly fixed. Operating expenses were $33.67 per BOE in the third quarter, inside the guidance range of $32.00 to $34.00, lease operating expense was $5.66 per BOE against $5.42 a year earlier, midstream operating expense rose to $3.89 per BOE from $2.56 with the Cardinal acquisition, and taxes other than income rose with revenue to $4.75 per BOE, so production taxes make part of the cost base move with price. Reported EBITDA margin was 63.95% over the last twelve months against 65.94% in FY2025, with the decline mainly from derivative losses reported within revenue. Management says well costs of $804 per completed lateral foot, 6% below a year earlier, offset service inflation, but the company also warns that higher oil prices may bring more service cost inflation, so margins compress when prices rise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high and the cash that remains is modest relative to EBITDA. Total capital expenditure guidance for 2026 is $1.67 billion to $1.73 billion, about 68.64% of last twelve months operating cash flow at the midpoint, free cash flow after organic spending was 0.28x of EBITDA, and fourth quarter capital spending is guided to $425 million to $485 million, a 19% rise on the third quarter. Flexibility is real because contractual drilling commitments were small, at USD 79,038 thousand for non-operated wells and USD 22,622 thousand for rigs at year-end 2025, and most drilling is operated and discretionary, but the Marlan processing expansion is underwritten by a new producer agreement and cannot be cut freely. EBITDA therefore turns into free cash flow of about USD 688,366 thousand a year, enough to fund the stated repayment of $350 million to $400 million and the new dividend rate, but not enough to absorb a further debt-funded acquisition without leverage rising again.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense among Delaware Basin producers, and Matador is a price taker whose differentiation is cost: well cost per completed lateral foot of $804 and a core acreage position, which was extended by more than 25,000 net acres across more than 1,100 transactions in 2025 and 2026, support margins but do not set prices. New entrants face a high capital and acreage barrier in the core basin, and substitutes are not a near-term credit factor, so those two forces do not change the view. Buyer power matters because three purchasers took 72% of 2025 revenue, and supplier power matters through oilfield service inflation and through takeaway capacity: natural gas prices were negative in the second quarter of 2026 until the Hugh Brinson pipeline opened, which shows that midstream constraints can erase gas revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two categories alter credit quality. Economic factors dominate because oil price moves of $10 per barrel change annual EBITDA by about $456.11 million on last twelve months volumes, which is 18.44% of reported EBITDA. Political and regulatory factors matter through federal leasing, since the May 2026 federal lease purchase of about $1.16 billion was a government sale, and through a regulatory burden that the company says raises costs and cannot be predicted. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are production scale and reserve life, interest cover of 11.29x, an integrated midstream system that gives flow assurance, access to bond and bank markets, and effective reporting and controls. Weaknesses are the 2026 step-up in leverage, hedges that cap upside, single-basin and purchaser concentration, non-recourse San Mateo debt with a 2027 maturity, and payouts that rise during the leverage build. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are free cash flow applied to the revolver, the Woodford play with about 50,000 net acres, long-term Gulf Coast gas sales from the first quarter of 2027 and a new 300 MMcf per day processing plant underwritten by a producer agreement. Threats are an oil price fall toward the 2025 average, a recurrence of negative gas pricing, a cut in the borrowing base at a redetermination, integration shortfalls and service cost inflation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ranked strengths. First, scale and reserve life: production of 230,470 BOE per day and reserves of 667.0 million BOE give a reserve life of 8.8 years, which spreads fixed costs and supports lender confidence in the borrowing base. Second, cash generation: LTM EBITDA of USD 2,474,028 thousand covers cash interest 11.29x, so a revenue shock must be large before interest is at risk. Third, integrated midstream: 720 MMcf per day of processing at San Mateo plus Cardinal gives flow assurance and fee income. Fourth, market access: the 2028 notes were replaced with 2034 notes at a 6.0% coupon and the Credit Agreement commitment was raised to $2.75 billion, so refinancing in 2026 was achievable. Fifth, reporting quality: effective controls and quarterly reconciliations support monitoring.

fields.value: Ranked weaknesses. First, acquisition-driven leverage: pro forma net debt of USD 6,147.402 million is 2.48x LTM EBITDA, so earnings from the acquired assets must arrive to restore the year-end 2025 level of 1.39x. Second, revolver headroom: about $446.9 million undrawn after Paloma leaves little room for a further shock. Third, hedge structure: ceilings below the realized price turn higher prices into cash losses while floors protect only part of the volume. Fourth, structural leakage and maturity at San Mateo: 33.20% of debt is non-recourse, 49% of distributions go to the partner and $650.0 million falls due on July 30, 2027. Fifth, concentration in one basin, one commodity and three purchasers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine financial-profile dimensions assess as follows. Scale and market position is strong on production, reserves and midstream capacity. Competitive advantage is average because cost per foot and acreage help but Matador is a price taker. Business diversification is weak because one basin supplies all oil and three purchasers take 72% of revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is average because drilling is discretionary but midstream expansion and acquired inventory create spending. Margin stability is average because the reported margin fell from 65.94% to 63.95% on derivative losses and costs per BOE rose. Free cash flow stability is average, with conversion of 0.28x of EBITDA. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average to strong on the 2026 notes refinancing and the 2029 revolver, tempered by the 2027 San Mateo maturity. Liquidity is average and declining after the Paloma borrowing. Financial policy and governance is average, because transparent reporting is offset by rising payouts, recurring EnCap-linked sellers and missing board information.

fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, interest cover and capital-market access; the constraints are leverage, headroom and concentration; the trend since year-end 2025 is weaker on leverage and liquidity and stronger on volume; and the key missing data are covenant definitions, the November 2026 redetermination, acquired earnings and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months management guides full-year 2026 production to 223,000 to 224,000 BOE per day, fourth quarter production to 238,000 to 242,000 BOE per day with Paloma and Ridge Runner adding about 10,000 BOE per day, and mid-single-digit growth or better in 2027, with long-term Gulf Coast gas sales beginning in the first quarter of 2027. These are tailwinds for revenue and for repayment if prices hold, and the 2026 collars roll off after the fourth quarter, reducing ceiling losses. Headwinds are the small 2027 hedge volume of 3,650,000 barrels, service cost inflation, possible negative gas pricing and the need to refinance San Mateo's $650.0 million term loan by July 30, 2027. Over three to five years the main uncertainties are integration of the added inventory, the Woodford play and the maturity of the revolvers in 2029 and the notes in 2032 to 2034.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside is a price reversion on a larger debt base. If realized oil prices fall from the $79.63 per barrel last twelve months average to the 2025 average of $64.99, revenue and EBITDA fall by about $667.7 million on last twelve months volumes before cost savings, while lower prices would stop the collar ceilings absorbing cash, which offsets at most the $239.08 million of realized derivative losses in the period, so pro forma net leverage would be between 3.01x and 3.40x against 2.48x. The first operational break would be cash flow after capital spending: the 2026 capital programme and the new dividend rate of about $216.56 million a year are largely committed in the short term, so the shortfall would be drawn on a revolver with about $446.9 million undrawn, and a lower price deck at the next redetermination could reduce the $3.25 billion borrowing base. Management levers are capital spending, which is discretionary, the dividend, the repurchase authority of USD 320,195 thousand, asset sales and non-core divestitures, and management says it does not expect to need equity markets; the observable triggers are the borrowing base, revolver availability, realized oil price and the San Mateo refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Matador presents an adequate business profile supported by production scale, a reserve life of 8.8 years, interest cover of 11.29x and integrated midstream, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-driven leverage, narrower revolver headroom, a hedge book that caps upside and non-recourse San Mateo debt with a 2027 maturity. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at current prices because LTM operating cash flow was USD 2,476,555 thousand, but it depends on oil prices holding well above the 2025 average. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on repaying the revolver as planned, on the borrowing base and on a long-term refinancing of the San Mateo term loan. The primary downside path is an oil price reversion on a larger debt base that draws the remaining revolver capacity. Further analysis would require covenant definitions, the redetermination result, acquired earnings and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: acquisition-driven leverage meeting a fall in oil prices.
